title: Bitwarden vault export and admin changes
volume: None on a normal day for exports and policies. Invites come with new starters, a few a week.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: Three custom detection rules for Bitwarden, on the CloudAudit records the library's Bitwarden parsers write from the organization event log. They make a detection when someone exports a vault, an admin changes an organization policy, or a member is invited. Each rule matches sensor type Bitwarden only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's Bitwarden parsers and the example bridge in bridges/bitwarden-events, and run the bridge with an organization API key, as the parser entry says. Then run the check-your-data search to see events arrive.

How it works:
- The parsers write the event name from Bitwarden's Public API, such as Organization_ClientExportedVault, and the acting member's email, which the bridge looks up, as the user.
- Bitwarden's event doesn't say which policy changed or how, so the policy rule takes every policy change. The policy ID is a resource on the record.
- Vault exports are on the event log only when the export ran in a Bitwarden app that sends events, which every official app does.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-23, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 8 records agreed. The samples went in with their dates moved to the day before the test, so they fell inside the search's time range.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines within about a minute. The lines went in 20 minutes after the rules were made, and every rule fired on the first send.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on the lines these rules take. Sophos's sign-in analytics flagged only sample sign-ins on Auth, as an unseen user, address or application.
- The events went in through bridges/bitwarden-events, run once on the lab machine against a local mock of the Bitwarden Public API that served the sample events, and posted to HTTP Ingest as gzipped NDJSON, the way the bridge's README says.

Known gaps:
- The bridge polls, so detections arrive up to one poll interval after the event.
- Bitwarden's apps send events about every 60 seconds, and a modified client could suppress them.
